## 453ac12fbe96

**Classification: suspected shortcut with a reproduced validator/domain gap.**
The canonical four pairs and every ordinary `_corner_poly` draw force all three
normalized objects to contain `(0,0)`. A learner can therefore implement the
reference overlap-count rule everywhere else but hard-code output `(0,0)=8`.
That rival fits the entire canonical set and ordinary generator distribution.

`checks/audit/453ac12fbe96/input.json` is a 7×15 input with three distinct,
connected, non-touching three-cell polyominoes. One object has normalized cells
`{(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)}`, so not all objects contain normalized `(0,0)`. The current
`self_check` nevertheless returns `[]` because it checks only the number of
foreground colors (`validator.json`). The supported Racket application gives
`[[2,8],[8,0]]`, while the shortcut gives `[[8,8],[8,0]]`
(`racket.json`, `rival.json`). The input is lawful for the reference program and
passes the current validator, but it is outside the generator's explicitly
restricted ordinary distribution. That restriction is exactly the teaching
risk; a future repair should generate some connected shapes whose normalized
bounding-box corner is empty and strengthen `self_check` to match the stated
object constraints.

Secondary documentation mismatch: `SUMMARY.md` says 3–4 cells and bounding box
at most 3, while `_corner_poly` currently draws 4–7 cells with bounding box up
to 5. I left this audit target unchanged.
